7day.d1.title: Arrival and a welcome dinner
7day.d1.travel: Meet and greet at the airport, private transfer to your hotel
7day.d1.body0: You're met at Cairo International Airport and taken to your hotel. There's no sightseeing today, just arrival. Cairo is a city of twenty million people, and an evening to take in its noise and pace isn't wasted. In the evening, a welcome dinner at a restaurant.
7day.d2.title: Giza, the Egyptian Museum and Khan el-Khalili
7day.d2.travel: Private transfers · overnight train Cairo → Aswan
7day.d2.pace: The longest day of the trip, with the most moving parts
7day.d2.seg0.text: The Giza plateau: the pyramids of Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure, built around 2500 BC, and the Great Sphinx below them.
7day.d2.seg1.text: The Egyptian Museum on Tahrir Square, one of the densest collections of pharaonic material anywhere: statuary, papyri and the Tanis royal gold. Lunch is at a local restaurant.
7day.d2.seg2.text: Khan el-Khalili, the bazaar quarter that has traded continuously since the fourteenth century. Then you board the overnight sleeper train south towards Aswan, with dinner served on board.
7day.d2.opt0: Inside one of the pyramids (Khufu, Khafre or Menkaure): a steep, narrow descent, extra ticket
7day.d2.opt1: The Mummies Room at the Egyptian Museum: extra ticket
7day.d2.opt2: The Grand Egyptian Museum (Tutankhamun's complete tomb contents) or the National Museum of Egyptian Civilisation (the royal mummies) instead of the Tahrir museum: extra cost, on request
7day.d3.title: Board the cruise: the High Dam, Philae and the Unfinished Obelisk
7day.d3.travel: Arrive by sleeper train · boat crossing to Philae
7day.d3.body0: You arrive in Aswan in the morning and board the Nile cruise ship that will be your hotel for the next three nights. Aswan sits where the Nile narrows towards the first cataract, and it's the country's most unhurried city.
7day.d3.body1: In the afternoon, the Aswan High Dam, completed in 1970: the project that controlled the annual flood and created Lake Nasser. Then the Temple of Philae, dedicated mainly to Isis and rebuilt block by block on Agilkia Island during the UNESCO rescue of the 1960s and 1970s. You reach it by a short boat crossing. Last, the Unfinished Obelisk, still lying in its granite quarry, abandoned around 1500 BC when a crack appeared in the stone.
7day.d4.title: Sailing north to Kom Ombo
7day.d4.pace: Relaxed sailing with a shore visit
7day.d4.body0: The most leisurely day of the trip. The cruise sails north from Aswan, and the hours on deck are as much the point as the stop: desert cliffs, palm-lined banks, the occasional village and heron.
7day.d4.body1: At Kom Ombo, a Ptolemaic temple built for two gods at once, Sobek the crocodile god and Horus the Elder, laid out in perfect symmetry with duplicate halls and sanctuaries for each. It also holds one of the few surviving ancient Egyptian calendars carved in relief, and a small museum of mummified crocodiles found nearby.
7day.d5.title: The Temple of Horus at Edfu
7day.d5.body0: The morning is spent at Edfu, the most completely preserved temple in Egypt, built between 237 and 57 BC. Its walls, roof, forecourt and inner sanctuary are largely intact, so you can follow the processional route from the open courtyard through the hypostyle hall to the sanctuary where the statue of Horus stood. Two granite falcons guard the entrance pylon, and the walls carry reliefs of the struggle between Horus and Set.
7day.d5.body1: The afternoon is unscheduled, and the ship reaches Luxor by evening.
7day.d6.title: The West Bank, Karnak and Luxor Temple, then the flight to Cairo
7day.d6.travel: Private transfers · domestic flight Luxor → Cairo · private transfer to your hotel
7day.d6.pace: The fullest day of the trip, with an early start
7day.d6.seg0.heading: Morning: the West Bank
7day.d6.seg0.text: The Valley of the Kings, with more than sixty royal tombs cut into the limestone and painted with scenes of the afterlife. Then the terraced Mortuary Temple of Hatshepsut at Deir el-Bahari, and the Colossi of Memnon, all that stands above ground of a once-enormous mortuary temple.
7day.d6.seg1.heading: Midday: the East Bank
7day.d6.seg1.text: Karnak, a temple city built and rebuilt over about 1,500 years. Its Great Hypostyle Hall has 134 columns rising to 21 metres. Lunch is at a local restaurant.
7day.d6.seg2.heading: Afternoon and evening
7day.d6.seg2.text: Luxor Temple, linked to Karnak by the Avenue of Sphinxes, then a domestic flight to Cairo. In the evening, Muizz Street in Old Cairo, the spine of the medieval Fatimid city and busy until late, followed by a farewell dinner at a restaurant.
7day.d6.meal2.label: farewell dinner
7day.d6.opt0: The tombs of Tutankhamun, Sety I and Ramses VI in the Valley of the Kings: extra tickets, one each
7day.d7.title: Departure
7day.d7.body0: A final breakfast and the transfer to Cairo International Airport.
7day.d7.opt0: With a late flight, a few more hours in Cairo can be arranged. This is an optional extra, planned around your flight time.
7day.intro.opening: A private week that runs the length of Egypt: Cairo, the sleeper train south, three nights on the Nile between Aswan and Luxor, and the temples of ancient Thebes. You won't see everything in seven days, and no one does. You will see Cairo, the river and Luxor in an order where each place adds context to the next.
7day.intro.whyRoute: You travel south from Cairo to Aswan by overnight sleeper train, then north along the Nile by cruise to Luxor, then back to Cairo by domestic flight. Sailing north, the current is with you, and each temple adds context for the one before. Aswan, Egypt's southernmost city and its most relaxed, makes an easy arrival point. Luxor's great concentrated monuments come last, on the fullest day of the trip. Cairo bookends the week: one short night at the start, one night at the end.
7day.intro.makeItYoursIntro: This is a private journey, built around your party. Common changes:
7day.stay.hotels: two nights in a five-star Cairo hotel. Standard is Hilton or Sheraton class. Deluxe (Kempinski or Fairmont class) and Luxury (Four Seasons or St. Regis class) are available on request.
7day.stay.river: three nights aboard a five-star cruise ship between Aswan and Luxor, full board.
7day.stay.train: the overnight train from Cairo to Aswan, with dinner and breakfast on board.
7day.stay.flight: a domestic flight from Luxor back to Cairo.
7day.stay.everyDay: a licensed English-speaking Egyptologist, and private air-conditioned transfers. The trip is private, operated for your party alone and never shared with a group.
7day.fit0: are visiting Egypt for the first time and want its essential route in one week
7day.fit1: prefer three nights on a cruise to moving between hotels
7day.fit2: have one week and want to spend it properly
7day.worth0: Days 2 and 6 are long and start early. That's what makes Cairo, the river and Luxor possible in seven days.
7day.worth1: Day 4 is slow by design, with most of it spent sailing.
7day.worth2: The pyramid interior, if you choose it, is a steep, narrow, airless descent.
7day.excl.itin7cairohrs: Extra hours in Cairo before a late departure: optional

7day.option2: Fly south instead of taking the sleeper train
7day.option3: Upgrade the hotels to Deluxe or Luxury class
giza.intro.opening: The pyramids of Giza in the morning, the Grand Egyptian Museum in the afternoon. In one private day you stand at the base of the largest stone structure ever built, go inside one of the pyramids, look the Great Sphinx in the face, and see Tutankhamun's complete burial equipment, displayed together for the first time. It's a full day, and it moves.
giza.intro.whyThisOrder: The plateau comes first, before the heat builds. The museum's air-conditioned halls come in the afternoon, when you'll want them. The 08:00 pickup is early for a reason: Cairo traffic is unpredictable, and the buffer it creates is real. Because the tour is private, your Egyptologist paces the day around you. Linger at Khufu, or move quickly across the plateau and save your energy for the museum.
giza.intro.returnNote: around 17:00–18:00, depending on your hotel's location
giza.fit0: are visiting for the first time and want the essential Cairo day done properly
giza.fit1: last visited before the Grand Egyptian Museum opened and want to see what has changed
giza.fit2: are travelling with older children who enjoy a well-told history day
giza.worth0: It's about nine hours. That's a lot for very young children.
giza.worth1: The plateau is uneven desert ground, and the pyramid passages are steep and narrow. The museum is very large. It's demanding for anyone with limited mobility.
giza.worth2: Cairo traffic can shift the times above. They're approximate.
giza.p0.label: The Giza Plateau
giza.p0.s0.title: Pickup from your hotel
giza.p0.s0.text: Your driver and Egyptologist collect you. On the way, your guide asks what matters most to you today (history, photography, pace) and plans the day around it.
giza.p0.s1.title: The three pyramids
giza.p0.s1.text: Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure were built within about eighty years of each other, around 2500 BC. They're the only surviving wonder of the ancient world. You start in front of the Great Pyramid of Khufu, 146 metres tall when it was finished. Then Khafre, the only one where some original casing stones survive near the top. Then Menkaure, the smallest, with granite casing brought from Aswan.
giza.p0.s1.included: Inside a pyramid (included). You go inside the pyramid of Khafre or Menkaure, subject to site rules and availability on the day.
giza.p0.s2.title: The panorama viewpoint
giza.p0.s2.text: A rise in the desert south-west of the plateau, where all three pyramids line up in one frame. This is the photography stop.
giza.p0.s3.title: The Great Sphinx and the Valley Temple
giza.p0.s3.text: The Sphinx, carved from the bedrock most probably under Khafre, and the Valley Temple beside it, one of the oldest stone buildings in Egypt. Your guide explains what the Sphinx meant to its builders and to the Egyptians who came after.
giza.p0.s4.title: Optional extras, if you've chosen them
giza.p0.s4.opt0: Inside the Great Pyramid of Khufu: extra ticket, subject to availability and site rules on the day
giza.p0.s4.opt1: A camel ride at the panorama area: extra cost.
giza.p0.s4.opt1.note: We work with handlers we know, whose animals are in good condition, and the ride is entirely your choice.
giza.p1.label: Lunch
giza.p1.s0.title: Lunch at a local restaurant (included)
giza.p1.s0.text: Chosen for quality and reliability. Dietary requirements can be catered for with advance notice. Drinks aren't included.
giza.p2.label: The Grand Egyptian Museum
giza.p2.s0.title: The Grand Egyptian Museum
giza.p2.s0.text: Fully open since 1 November 2025, at the north-east edge of the plateau. It's the largest archaeological museum in the world by floor area, so the visit is focused, not comprehensive. The centrepiece is the Tutankhamun galleries: his complete burial equipment, reassembled for the first time, including the golden throne, the shrines, the canopic equipment and the chariots. After that, your guide follows your interests: Old Kingdom statuary, everyday objects, the grand staircase lined with royal statues.
giza.p2.s1.title: Back to your hotel
giza.p2.s1.text: Around 17:00 if you're staying near the pyramids, later for central Cairo. You're back in time to freshen up before dinner, and your guide can suggest an evening plan if you'd like one.
